title: Peterbot rejoint shxrk et t3eny, un trio de rêve pour les FNCS 2027
content:
C’est l’un des premiers gros coups du mercato Fortnite pour 2027. L’Américain Peter « Peterbot » Kata, sacré champion du monde FNCS en 2024, va unir ses forces avec le Roumain Oltean « shxrk » Ștefan et le Slovène Tin « t3eny » Popovic, tous deux sous contrat avec Aurora Gaming. Un rapprochement qui n’était pas forcément attendu, puisque shxrk et t3eny semblaient initialement partis pour poursuivre leur aventure avec Swizzy. Mais ce dernier ne fera finalement pas partie du trio, ouvrant la porte à l’arrivée de l’une des plus grandes stars de la scène compétitive.

Ce changement représente un véritable tournant pour les deux vice-champions du monde. Après avoir brillé sur la scène internationale en 2026, shxrk et t3eny tenteront désormais de franchir la dernière marche avec Peterbot. Sur le papier, l’association réunit trois joueurs capables de rivaliser avec les meilleurs, mais leur complémentarité reste à démontrer. L’arrivée d’une nouvelle personnalité au sein d’un duo déjà bien établi pourrait notamment nécessiter quelques ajustements dans leur manière de jouer.

Si certains observateurs s’interrogent sur la capacité des trois joueurs à évoluer ensemble, Clix ne partage pas ces inquiétudes. Le streamer et joueur américain s’est montré particulièrement enthousiaste à l’annonce de cette association. « Je ne vois pas comment ce trio pourrait ne pas fonctionner. Les trois sont capables de s’adapter les uns aux autres » , a-t-il déclaré.

De son côté, Swizzy pourrait également retrouver une équipe de premier plan. Double champion du monde en titre, il serait désormais susceptible de rejoindre Vic0 et Malibuca, une autre association qui pourrait faire parler d’elle lors des prochaines FNCS. Cette piste reste toutefois à confirmer.

Avec Peterbot, shxrk et t3eny réunis sous les mêmes couleurs, la saison 2027 de Fortnite s’annonce déjà particulièrement intéressante. Reste à voir si ce trio parviendra à transformer son immense potentiel individuel en résultats collectifs, avec un objectif évident : décrocher le titre mondial.

PETERBOT REJOINT SHXRK ET T3ENY POUR LES FNCS TRIO C’EST QUOI CE RETOURNEMENT DE SITUATION ??? Shxrk vient d’annoncer que Swizzy ne jouera PLUS avec eux… ET C’EST PETERBOT QUI LE REMPLACE PETERBOT SHXRK T3ENY pic.twitter.com/Z38Dupom67

title: Yike révèle le secret du comeback de la Karmine Corp
content:
La Karmine Corp a réussi son entrée aux Worlds 2026, mais elle s’est fait très peur. Bousculés par Cloud9, les Français ont dû revenir au score à deux reprises pour finalement s’imposer au terme de cinq manches. Une victoire arrachée au mental, comme l’a expliqué Martin « Yike » Sundelin dans un entretien accordé à L’Équipe . Le jungler suédois reconnaît notamment les difficultés rencontrées en début de partie, face à des Américains mieux préparés et particulièrement agressifs. « Tout le match a été assez bordélique » , admet-il, conscient que la KC devra rapidement corriger ses erreurs.

Mais cette rencontre a surtout permis de mesurer les progrès réalisés depuis la lourde défaite contre Movistar KOI (0-3), lors des playoffs du LEC. Après cette élimination, les joueurs avaient longuement échangé sur leur fonctionnement collectif et leur capacité à réagir dans les moments difficiles. « Ces dernières semaines, nous avions beaucoup parlé de notre gestion des défaites, nous voulions vraiment progresser là-dessus » , raconte Yike. Un travail poursuivi lors du bootcamp en Corée du Sud, où chacun a été invité à prendre davantage ses responsabilités.

C'EST NOTRE DRAGON, TRIPLE KILL POUR NOUS #KCORP pic.twitter.com/k8P3dvxrFV

Face à Cloud9, ces efforts ont visiblement porté leurs fruits. Malgré deux manches perdues de manière inquiétante, la Karmine Corp n’a jamais abandonné. « Même après nos manches perdues, on a réussi à revenir au mental, en gardant nos têtes hautes » , souligne le Suédois. Un changement d’attitude qu’il considère comme l’une des principales raisons de cette victoire. Yike insiste également sur le rôle de Reapered, particulièrement actif entre les parties pour identifier les problèmes et ajuster le plan de jeu. Le jungler estime que le coaching staff a beaucoup mieux géré ces moments que lors de la défaite contre KOI, permettant aux joueurs de rester concentrés malgré les difficultés.

Tout n’est cependant pas réglé. Le Suédois reconnaît que la pression a pesé sur les premières manches et regrette son propre manque d’initiative, notamment sur Lee Sin. Mais il reste optimiste pour la suite : « On veut tous s’améliorer et je pense que nous allons être encore meilleurs. »

La Karmine Corp devra désormais confirmer ces progrès face à MVK Esports, son prochain adversaire dans le Play-In. Encore à deux victoires en BO5 de la phase suisse, les Français devront afficher un visage plus convaincant pour poursuivre leur aventure aux Worlds 2026.

title: VCT EMEA : nAts sur le départ de Team Liquid ?
content:
L’avenir de nAts chez Team Liquid est désormais incertain. Ayaz « nAts » Akhmetshin a annoncé sur X être à la recherche d’une équipe pour la saison 2027 de VALORANT. Une déclaration qui pourrait marquer la fin d’une collaboration de quatre ans avec l’organisation, même si aucun départ n’a encore été officialisé. « Je suis toujours en discussions avec Team Liquid, mais l’organisation m’a également autorisé à explorer mes options pour l’année prochaine » , a précisé le joueur russe. Capable d’évoluer comme IGL ou Sentinelle, il se dit ouvert aux propositions de toutes les régions du VCT.

Arrivé chez Liquid fin 2022, nAts s’est imposé comme l’un des piliers de l’équipe, aussi bien par ses performances individuelles que par son leadership. En quatre saisons, il a participé à sept compétitions internationales et remporté deux titres en VCT EMEA. Malgré les nombreux changements d’effectif traversés par l’organisation, le Russe est resté une pièce centrale du projet, confirmant son statut parmi les joueurs les plus expérimentés de la région.

Avant son arrivée chez Team Liquid, nAts s’était déjà fait un nom sur la scène internationale avec Gambit Esports. Vainqueur des Masters Berlin en 2021, il avait également atteint la finale des Champions la même année, s’inclinant face à Acend. Des performances qui avaient fait de lui l’un des meilleurs joueurs du monde à son poste.

Alors que plusieurs organisations préparent déjà leur effectif pour la saison 2027, la disponibilité potentielle d’un joueur de son calibre pourrait animer le mercato. Son expérience du plus haut niveau, sa polyvalence et ses qualités de leader représentent autant d’atouts pour les équipes à la recherche d’un nouveau capitaine.

Reste désormais à savoir si Team Liquid parviendra à convaincre nAts de prolonger l’aventure ou si le Russe choisira de relever un nouveau défi. Pour l’heure, toutes les options restent ouvertes, y compris celle d’une cinquième saison sous les couleurs de Liquid.

LFT for the 2027 VCT season I’m still in talks with Team Liquid, but they’ve also given me permission to explore my options for next year. Main roles: IGL / Sentinel Open to opportunities across all VCT regions. Contact: offnats@gmail.com pic.twitter.com/nZ7HockjlM

title: FIFAe Finals postponed on eve of Jeddah tournament
content:
FIFA and the Saudi Esports Federation postponed the 2026 FIFAe Finals on October 15, one day before the Jeddah event was due to begin, with no replacement date or venue announced.

The decision leaves national teams and event partners without a confirmed schedule for the competition, which had been planned for October 16–25 at Abadi Al Johar Arena. The joint statement cited an assessment of regional developments and their effect on the logistical arrangements required to stage the tournament; it did not mention security.

Japan’s football association said on October 10 that it would not send its team after assessing safety and security in the host country. Brazil’s football confederation later cancelled the eSeleção’s participation, citing regional tensions and risks involving the airspace and airports its delegation would use.

FIFA’s September 1 qualification announcement said more than 120 nations had entered, with teams qualifying through five in-person continental championships. The scheduled field comprised 12 national teams in each of the console and mobile eFootball competitions, plus 16 in Rocket League .

FIFA’s September announcement did not state a 2026 prize pool. The previous edition, held in 2025, had a $450,000 prize pool, according to FIFA.

The FIFAe delay follows other changes to major esports events planned for Saudi Arabia. The 2026 Esports World Cup moved from Riyadh to Paris in May, while the inaugural Esports Nations Cup was postponed from November 2026 to November 2027 after most qualifying had taken place. Organisers said Saudi Arabia remained capable of hosting events.

The Nations Cup delay has also left national teams and players facing uncertainty over replacement plans, while the World Cup move provides a recent example of a Saudi-hosted event changing location. FIFA and the Saudi Esports Federation had confirmed the FIFAe Finals for 2025 and 2026 in a July 2025 announcement; the current hosting and publisher arrangements are described as covering those two years.

Those schedule changes add uncertainty to the 2026 esports tournament calendar . The separate Esports Nations Cup postponement also illustrates the planning challenges created when national-team competitions lose their original dates.

FIFA said further announcements would follow in due course, but has not confirmed whether the Finals will remain in Jeddah or elsewhere in Saudi Arabia. It is also unclear whether qualification results will carry over, how organisers will handle travel and venue costs already incurred, or whether Japan and Brazil could participate if the event is rescheduled.

The status of the hosting and publisher agreements would also need clarification if the tournament moves beyond 2026. For now, FIFA will not crown its console eFootball, mobile eFootball and Rocket League world champions in October; the next announcement is expected to address the event’s replacement arrangements.

title: Joblife prépare un roster avec soulcas et hoody pour Project Blender
content:
Joblife commence à préparer son avenir sur VALORANT. Après une saison 2026 marquée par deux titres en Challengers France et une participation aux Play-Ins du VCT EMEA, l’organisation française devrait profiter de Project Blender pour tester plusieurs nouvelles recrues. D’après les informations de Sheep Esports , soulcas, hoody, Sevire et WanZeru devraient rejoindre runneR, seul rescapé de l’effectif précédent, pour disputer la deuxième phase de la compétition. Le groupe serait encadré par pakko, ancien entraîneur de Gentle Mates, dont l’arrivée a été officialisée le 7 octobre.

Parmi les noms annoncés, soulcas et hoody apporteraient une solide expérience du plus haut niveau européen. Passé notamment par Team Liquid et Apeks, soulcas retrouverait la compétition après une année presque entièrement passée loin des serveurs. De son côté, hoody, ancien joueur de G2 Esports et Giants, sort d’une saison particulièrement active sur le circuit secondaire. Le Britannique Sevire connaît également bien la scène française, après des passages chez Solary, Karmine Corp Blue Stars et Mandatory, avec qui il a notamment atteint les finales des Challengers France et EMEA au printemps. Enfin, le jeune Tchèque WanZeru, 19 ans, arriverait de Team Liquid Academy, où il a évolué durant la saison 2026.

Ce nouveau cinq ne serait toutefois pas nécessairement définitif. Les joueurs peuvent en effet participer à Project Blender sans être sous contrat, ce qui permettrait à Joblife d’évaluer plusieurs profils avant de prendre ses décisions pour 2027. Les joueurs concernés resteraient donc disponibles sur le marché, et des changements ne sont pas à exclure dans les prochaines semaines.

Directement invitée en deuxième phase, Joblife retrouvera notamment NAVI, Eternal Fire, l’Eintracht Francfort et CGN Esports. Les huit équipes seront réparties en deux groupes de quatre, avec des rencontres en BO3. Les deux premières de chaque groupe accéderont aux playoffs, avant une demi-finale décisive pour rejoindre la troisième et dernière phase du tournoi, dont la finale en LAN est prévue à Paris.

Pour Joblife, l’objectif sera double : confirmer les progrès réalisés en 2026 et poser les bases d’un effectif capable de rivaliser avec les meilleures équipes européennes en 2027. Après avoir notamment battu Fnatic, NAVI et PCIFIC Esports lors des Play-Ins du VCT EMEA, la structure française espère poursuivre sur sa lancée avec un groupe profondément renouvelé.

title: La Karmine Corp se fait peur… mais réussit son entrée aux Worlds 2026
content:
Pour ses premiers pas aux championnats du monde de League of Legends, la Karmine Corp est passée par toutes les émotions. Opposée à Cloud9, troisième représentant nord-américain, l’équipe française a vécu un début de BO5 cauchemardesque. Dès la première manche, les Américains ont infligé une véritable correction à la KC, avec un score sans appel de 20-1 aux kills. Sur la midlane, Loki s’est montré absolument intouchable, terminant la partie en 11/0/3 sur Locke. Une entrée en matière inquiétante, qui a rapidement fait ressurgir les difficultés aperçues lors des playoffs du Summer Split.

Car au-delà du résultat, c’est surtout le jeu collectif de la Karmine Corp qui a posé problème. Souvent en retard sur les objectifs, les Français ont peiné à coordonner leurs déplacements et à trouver les bonnes ouvertures lors des teamfights. Des hésitations particulièrement coûteuses face à une équipe de Cloud9 capable d’accélérer brutalement en milieu de partie. La deuxième manche a d’ailleurs failli tourner à une nouvelle démonstration, avec Loki toujours aussi dangereux sur Akali (5/2/1) et Tactical largement en avance sur Kalista (6/1/5). Mais cette fois, la KC a réussi l’impensable : un teamfight décisif autour du dragon, porté par le duo kyeahoo-Caliste, lui a permis de renverser une partie pourtant très mal engagée.

C'EST TOUT DROIT ! pic.twitter.com/ZgwtDeCjHX

Ce sursaut n’a toutefois pas immédiatement réglé les problèmes des Français. Dans la troisième manche, Cloud9 a repris sa domination avec une victoire écrasante, 22-5 aux kills, sous l’impulsion d’un Blaber impérial sur Jarvan IV (7/0/14). Dos au mur, la Karmine Corp devait impérativement réagir pour éviter une élimination dès son entrée en lice.

Et c’est Caliste qui a relancé les siens. Auteur d’une prestation exceptionnelle sur Xayah (11/1/3), le jeune ADC français a notamment fait basculer un teamfight crucial avant que la KC ne sécurise le dragon ancestral et n’égalise à 2-2. Tout allait donc se jouer dans une cinquième manche décisive, au son des traditionnels Silver Scrapes.

YESSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSS pic.twitter.com/h9ev2J76pB

Cette fois, les Français ont affiché un tout autre visage. Avec un Yike retrouvé dans la jungle et un excellent kyeahoo sur la midlane, la Karmine Corp a maîtrisé cette dernière partie pour arracher une victoire aussi précieuse que spectaculaire. Le midlaner coréen aura d’ailleurs été l’une des grandes satisfactions de la rencontre, capable de tenir son rang même lorsque son équipe traversait ses moments les plus difficiles.

ON VA VIRER LES NA ! pic.twitter.com/swY3eapym1

Grâce à ce succès (3-2), la Karmine Corp poursuit son aventure dans le Play-In des Worlds 2026, mais le chemin vers le Main Event est encore long. Les Français devront remporter deux nouveaux BO5, à commencer par un affrontement contre la formation vietnamienne MVK Esports, qui a collé un 3-0 à FURIA. Après s’être fait très peur face à Cloud9, la bande à Kameto devra rapidement corriger ses problèmes de coordination et de gestion des objectifs pour espérer décrocher son billet pour la phase suisse.

Victoire 3-2 face à Cloud 9 ! Elle était pas évidente à aller chercher mais on a vu notre équipe step up tout au long du BO pour décrocher cette victoire ! #KCORP GG @Cloud9 pic.twitter.com/pSaenHwvjw

title: Only one Dane remains in Astralis’ new CS2 lineup
content:
Astralis has signed siuhy and cmtry , completing its first international Counter-Strike 2 lineup and ending the organisation’s all-Danish roster era.

The signings of Kamil “siuhy” Szkaradek and Nikita “cmtry” Samolotov were reported by Dust2.us and HLTV on October 13. They follow the October 9 benching of Rasmus “HooXi” Nielsen and Jakob “jabbi” Nygaard, which left two places to fill in Astralis’ active five.

Siuhy joins after serving as an in-game leader at Team Liquid. Astralis’ announcement confirms his signing but does not specify whether he will take on the same leadership role in the new lineup; he became a free agent earlier in October, according to HLTV.

Cmtry, who previously AWPed for NAVI Junior and FUT, is expected to switch to a rifling role. The move restores Astralis to five active players, with Filip “NEO” Kubski continuing as coach. It follows the benching of HooXi and jabbi and siuhy’s departure from Liquid.

The lineup comprises Victor “Staehr” Staehr, Love “phzy” Smidebrant, Gytis “ryu” Glušauskas, siuhy and cmtry, with NEO as coach. Staehr is the sole Dane in the five, a major change for a club that won four Major trophies with an all-Danish lineup.

The international roster marks a new chapter in Astralis’ Counter-Strike identity, rather than a continuation of its previous national core. The club’s October roster changes set the stage for the shift, with the additions of a former Liquid leader and a young rifler restoring the squad’s numbers.

Astralis had already secured a place at the PGL Singapore Major after its previous lineup won Stake Ranked Episode 4, beating Nemiga in the final. The new players need to play five matches before the Major invite cutoff to qualify for in-game stickers, according to Dust2.us.

Stake Pulse Beat III and Stake Ranked Episode 5 are the listed opportunities to reach that threshold. Astralis’ first scheduled outing with the new roster was against Sashi in the opening match of Stake Pulse Beat III on October 14, in Group C.

title: Eight teams chase $1m at Thunderpick World Championship in Malta
content:
Thunderpick World Championship 2026 is an eight-team CS2 event with a $1 million prize pool, featuring headline organisations FURIA, Team Falcons and Aurora Gaming in Malta from October 14-18.

The tournament is taking place at BLAST Arena Studios. Seven teams received invitations based on Valve Regional Standings (VRS) rankings, while one qualified through a global qualifier, according to esports.gg. Virtus.pro could not attend because of visa issues, and Ninjas in Pyjamas took its place.

The field and prize pool put the event among the major stops on the CS2 calendar, where tournament formats and financial scale help shape opportunities for teams and commercial partners. Thunderpick’s championship sits within a busy Counter-Strike tournament calendar , alongside established events run by other organisers.

The group stage uses double-elimination brackets, with the top two teams in each group advancing to the playoffs. The tournament’s opening results had already produced wins for 9z, Falcons, Legacy and FURIA on Wednesday, October 14.

The opening day saw 9z beat Aurora 2-0, Falcons defeat Ninjas in Pyjamas 2-0, Legacy sweep PARIVISION and FURIA take a 2-0 win over BetBoom. Those results set up advancement and elimination matches for the next group-stage day.

The event’s field combines organisations with recent competitive success, but the schedule also presents a challenge: esports.gg noted that some top organisations skipped the tournament because of calendar pressure. The competition therefore offers a substantial prize pool while placing the remaining teams in a compact five-day format.

Prize money is one part of the commercial picture for top CS2 tournaments, with event income and team opportunities also connected to broader revenue streams around competition. Esports Insider has examined how prize pools and sticker revenue intersect at the IEM Cologne Major .

The group stage runs through October 16, before the playoff bracket begins on October 17. Official Thunderpick esports channels are broadcasting matches on YouTube and Twitch, with the grand final scheduled for October 18.

title: Riot adds senior leaders for VALORANT, creators and TFT esports
content:
Riot Games has appointed Joe Lee as VALORANT Game Director and brought Mitchel Inkrott into the company as Global Head of Influencer Strategy, with both moves surfacing in October 2026.

Lee shared his appointment on LinkedIn on 11 October, according to reporting by bo3.gg. The outlet also reported that Lee had previously worked on VALORANT, but neither report establishes how his new position fits into the game’s leadership structure.

Lee has spent more than nine years at Riot. His most recent role was Senior Director of Product Management, following director-level positions in product management and strategic advisory, and earlier work spanning research, data analysis and revenue strategy.

Lee’s interest in VALORANT dates to an early playtest when the game was being developed under the codename Ares, according to Shane the Gamer. The appointment coverage does not detail his day-to-day remit or explain how it may affect game updates or competitive balance.

Inkrott joined Riot in October, after his Electronic Arts role ended in September. His previous work includes creator and influencer strategy positions at EA, marketing agency Ayzenberg and publisher 2K; at EA, his responsibilities covered Battlefield and other first-person shooter franchises, according to Shane the Gamer.

The three senior appointments reported during the same stretch of October span game leadership, creator strategy and competitive operations:

Lee and Inkrott’s specific responsibilities have not been set out in the appointment coverage. Inkrott said he had wanted to join Riot after following its player engagement, creator campaigns and esports scene. He is expected to work with Erin Wayne and the wider team, and plans to use his first few weeks to settle into the role.

Creator reach has a commercial role in esports beyond individual campaigns, including how tournament audiences engage with broadcasts. The debate over co-streaming and tournament viewership reflects that broader relationship between creators and competition audiences.

The immediate next step stated for Inkrott is onboarding with Wayne and Riot’s wider team. No specific changes to VALORANT’s creative direction, updates or balance have been detailed alongside Lee’s appointment, leaving those areas outside the confirmed scope of the announcements.

title: China’s VCT partner field set to shrink ahead of 2027
content:
Sheep Esports reports that eight organisations are expected to partner with VCT China in 2027 and 2028, as Riot Games reduces the number of partner teams from 10 to eight across its regions.

The reported lineup is EDward Gaming , JD Gaming , Bilibili Gaming , TYLOO , All Gamers , Trace Esports , Xi Lai Gaming and Weibo Gaming . The list is based on sources cited by Sheep Esports; Riot has not officially confirmed the teams or announced the full details of the China format.

Xi Lai Gaming is expected to move from a guest slot into the partner group after winning Ascension in 2024. Sheep Esports reports that the team has played at every international LAN since Masters Toronto 2025.

Weibo Gaming is also expected to return to the group. The organisation did not secure a partner slot in 2023 and later left VALORANT before returning to the scene in early 2026.

Four current partners are reported to miss the next cycle: FunPlus Phoenix , Nova Esports , Titan Esports Club and Wolves Esports . Dragon Ranger Gaming , which held a guest slot like XLG, is also reported to have been left out.

The reported changes would reshape which organisations have partner status, but losing that status would not necessarily end a team’s route to major events. The wider relationship between VALORANT’s Tier 1 and Tier 2 scenes remains relevant as Riot moves towards a more open competitive year.

The first VCT partnership cycle began in 2023 and concludes after the 2026 season. Riot is set to reduce partner numbers from 10 to eight in China, as in the other regions, while making the 2027 competitive year more open. The primary report says teams outside the partner group may still qualify for Cups and Masters events by building successful projects.

EDward Gaming is among the reported partners after winning Champions 2024, which Sheep Esports describes as China’s only international title since the current circuit began. Wolves, meanwhile, is set to miss out despite its surprise showing at Masters Toronto 2025. Chinese organisations’ recent competitive position also provides context for the reported partnership changes .

The route back for non-partner teams will depend on rules Riot has yet to spell out. Sheep Esports reports that China’s format may differ from those in the other three regions, leaving qualification mechanics unresolved; the lineup should therefore be treated as a report, not a confirmed Riot announcement.

title: A fourth ESL Pro League title lifts Vitality to prize-money summit
content:
Team Vitality beat MOUZ 3-0 in the ESL Pro League Season 24 grand final, moving above Natus Vincere in Counter-Strike’s all-time prize-money rankings. Vitality’s listed total is $13,886,593, a lead of $204,133 over NAVI’s $13,682,460.

The result put Vitality first in the historical standings, based on prize-money figures attributed to Liquipedia and dated October 12, 2026. The organisation entered the final with $13,591,593, approximately $91,000 behind NAVI, according to Pley.gg’s report.

The series was a sweep, but MOUZ pushed Vitality to overtime on Dust2 after reaching match point. Vitality took Cache 13-8 and Inferno 13-7 before closing Dust2 16-12 to secure the title.

The top five organisations in the reported all-time prize-money table are:

The Season 24 trophy was Vitality’s fourth ESL Pro League title, making it the first organisation to win the competition more than three times. NAVI, MOUZ, Astralis and Fnatic have three titles apiece. Vitality has won three of the last four seasons, with NAVI taking Season 23 in March.

Robin ‘ropz’ Kool claimed a record sixth ESL Pro League title, having won with MOUZ, FaZe Clan and Vitality. Mathieu ‘ZywOo’ Herbaut was named event MVP, his 34th career MVP award according to HLTV, and finished the final with a 1.65 rating.

Vitality’s wider leadership and brand ambitions form a separate part of the organisation’s growth story, while NAVI remains a leading name in the Counter-Strike scene.

Vitality’s next scheduled event is PGL Bucharest. A predicted VRS update after the final placed Vitality first and MOUZ second, although Valve’s official rankings update monthly. The all-time prize-money order may shift again as teams compete in upcoming events, but the current standings put Vitality at the top.

title: Major MVP m0NESY stays at Falcons through 2030
content:
Team Falcons have extended Ilya “m0NESY” Osipov ’s contract through 2030, retaining the Russian AWPer after he helped the team win the IEM Cologne Major and claimed the event’s MVP award. The organisation announced the multi-year agreement on Monday, October 12, according to HLTV.

The extension gives Falcons continuity around one of its central players as it builds on its first Major title. Neither Falcons’ announcement nor HLTV’s report disclosed the financial terms of the agreement.

m0NESY joined Falcons in April 2025 from G2 Esports in what HLTV described as a blockbuster move. He has averaged a 1.29 rating during his time with the team, according to the outlet.

The 21-year-old waited for his first trophy with Falcons, but the breakthrough came on the biggest stage: the team won the IEM Cologne Major in June, and m0NESY was named the tournament’s MVP. His extension keeps that star power in place as Falcons pursue further titles.

Falcons’ roster also includes Finn “karrigan” Andersen , Nikola “NiKo” Kovač , René “TeSeS” Madsen and Maksim “kyousuke” Lukin , with Danny “zonic” Sørensen as coach. The club’s wider Counter-Strike project and roster have featured in coverage of Falcons’ CS2 ambitions , while its Major campaign put its headline talent in the spotlight.

The Cologne victory gives Falcons a title to defend, with the next edition of the Major set to take place in Singapore, according to HLTV. The extension means m0NESY will remain part of the team’s plans as it targets that defence.

Falcons’ next event is the Thunderpick World Championship , which begins on October 14. IEM Beijing is also on the team’s calendar ahead of the Major. The team’s Cologne success was covered in reporting on Falcons’ Major-winning run ; its immediate focus now shifts to the Thunderpick tournament.

title: LOUD secure Vitality rematch after playoff upset
content:
LOUD beat NRG 2-1 in the VCT Champions 2026 upper-bracket semi-final on Saturday 10 October, advancing to face Team Vitality while NRG dropped into the lower bracket, according to Esports News UK.

The result gives LOUD another chance against the only team to beat them at the tournament so far. NRG, featuring British player Keiko, remain in contention but now have no room for error in the lower bracket.

LOUD claimed the opening map in 46 minutes, but NRG answered with the longest contest of the series, taking map two after 49 minutes to level the score. The match went to a decider, where LOUD closed out the series in 36 minutes.

The three-map win extends LOUD’s run to three consecutive victories at Champions. They had opened with a 2-0 win over EDward Gaming, then lost 0-2 to Vitality before recovering with 2-0 results against Global Esports and Paper Rex ahead of the NRG match.

NRG’s defeat ended a three-match winning streak at the event. The defending side had beaten Nongshim RedForce 2-0, Karmine Corp 2-1 and T1 2-0 before meeting LOUD, but the loss changes its route through the playoffs rather than ending its tournament.

LOUD advance to the upper-bracket final against Vitality, who reached the meeting with a 2-0 win over G2 Esports. NRG move into the lower bracket alongside teams still fighting to stay alive, including T1 and 100 Thieves, both of whom survived the first round there.

100 Thieves advanced by beating Nongshim RedForce 2-1, while T1 defeated Paper Rex by the same score. NRG will meet T1 again after beating them 2-0 in the upper-bracket quarter-final. The results leave multiple playoff paths open, with NRG needing to win each subsequent series to continue.

The split between the upper and lower brackets also shapes the tournament’s closing schedule. LOUD’s route offers a direct chance to reach the grand final, while NRG must first navigate the lower-bracket field. The Champions Shanghai format and schedule frame the stakes as the remaining teams approach the final days.

The upset stands out against the pre-match ratings reported by Esports News UK: NRG were 12th in the Elo power rankings with a 1,791 rating and a 73-36 record across 109 rated matches. LOUD were 51st, rated 1,672, with a 29-37 record over 66 matches.

The teams had split their four previous meetings in 2026, but the latest result gives LOUD back-to-back wins over NRG. Their upcoming Vitality fixture is a rematch of the earlier group-stage meeting, which Vitality won 2-0; the upper-bracket picture now puts that opponent between LOUD and a place in the final.

LOUD and Vitality are scheduled to meet on Friday 16 October, with Champions set to conclude on 18 October. The next match will determine which side advances directly to the grand final and which must continue through the lower bracket.

title: Watson powers Yandex to BLAST Slam VIII grand final win
content:
Team Yandex defeated Team Spirit 3-1 in the BLAST Slam VIII grand final, claiming a second consecutive major tournament title at the start of the 2026-2027 Dota 2 season.

Spirit took the opening game after 40 minutes, building a 48-19 kill advantage. Illya “Yatoro” Mulyarchuk led the way on Ursa with 19 kills and 12 assists, while Yandex were unable to recover after Spirit disrupted their early progress.

Yandex levelled the series in game two, converting a major teamfight win at the 23-minute mark into a 52-minute victory. Ammar “ATF” Assaf’s Timbersaw was central to the comeback, finishing with 20 kills and seven assists as Yandex’s core of ATF, Alimzhan “Watson” Islambekov and Ilya “CHIRA_JUNIOR” Chirtsov found their footing.

Watson then delivered a perfect 14-kill, 14-assist performance on Nature’s Prophet in game three. Yandex took control against Spirit’s slower lineup and secured the map after 48 minutes, moving one win from the title.

The final game lasted 56 minutes, with Yandex closing out the 3-1 result. Watson finished with 19 kills and 14 assists, while ATF added 13 kills and 22 assists; together, they helped Yandex finish with a 51-37 kill lead. GosuGamers reported the game-by-game results, while Field Level Media also reported the 3-1 final score.

The title adds to Yandex’s earlier success at BLAST Slam VIII , where the team had advanced through the playoff bracket to reach the championship match. The BLAST Slam VIII playoff field also saw Spirit fight through the lower bracket to set up the final.

Yandex claimed the tournament’s top prize, while Spirit finished runner-up. The result marked Yandex’s second BLAST title after BLAST Slam VII and delivered the first two major tournament wins of the 2026-2027 competitive season, according to GosuGamers.

Spirit entered the final as the reigning The International champions. Their second-place finish brought US$135,000, while Yandex collected US$270,000 for the championship.

The grand final was the teams’ third meeting at BLAST Slam VIII. Spirit had won their earlier seeding match, but Yandex claimed the next encounter with a sweep to become the first team through to the final.

Spirit reached the championship match after recovering from a deficit against PARIVISION in the lower-bracket final. Yandex’s win followed its PGL Wallachia Season 9 title in late September, giving the team consecutive major tournament victories.

GosuGamers also identified ATF’s arrival after Team Falcons exited the scene as a major move in the post-TI 2026 roster shuffle. The signing formed part of the roster context around Yandex’s run; its wider roster changes involving ATF preceded the team’s back-to-back tournament wins.

Yandex now heads into the next major cycle with two titles to open the season, while Spirit leave BLAST Slam VIII as runners-up after their first appearance with a changed roster. Their next meetings will offer another test of the matchup established across three encounters in Malta.

title: Tidebound Reunites Four TI 2025 Players for 2026-2027 Return
content:
Team Tidebound has returned to competitive Dota 2 after a 10-month hiatus, with Ning “ xiao8 ” Zhang coaching its roster for the 2026-2027 season.

The lineup brings back four players from Tidebound’s The International 2025 roster: carry Xuanang “ Shiro ” Guo, mid laner Cheng “ NothingToSay ” Jin Xiang, position 4 support Hao “ plAnet ” Lin and position 5 support Yiping “ y` ” Zhang. Veteran offlaner Haiyang “ Yang ” Zhou completes the five-player team.

GosuGamers reported that Tidebound shared the roster through its official Weibo account. The organisation had been inactive since December 2025, after placing seventh-eighth at TI 2025.

The roster combines its four returning players with Yang in the offlane, while xiao8 takes the coaching role. Tidebound’s announcement marks its return to competition following the 10-month break.

The return is among the latest developments in the post-TI 2026 roster shuffle. According to GosuGamers, xiao8 and NothingToSay last competed for Xtreme Gaming . xiao8 departed before TI 2026, while NothingToSay was released in early September after the team failed to advance from the group stage.

Shiro and y` most recently played for Vici Gaming , which disbanded after losing in the TI 2026 elimination stage. Team Resilience was plAnet’s previous team; he left in late August after its elimination-stage defeat.

Yang last represented Team Refuser , which finished fourth in the Chinese regional qualifier and missed TI 2026. The new Tidebound lineup therefore reunites four players from the organisation’s previous International roster while adding an offlaner from another team in the Chinese scene.

The roster’s return puts Tidebound back in the competition as teams rebuild for the 2026-2027 season. Its next appearances will establish when the lineup makes its competitive debut.
